problem_statement: A DTLS server socket can only maintain a single client session at a time: it keeps one TLS/DTLS context per socket file descriptor, so a second peer connecting to the same server socket cannot establish its own handshake, and traffic from multiple peers is not routed independently. A DTLS server socket should be able to handle several clients concurrently, maintaining a separate TLS session per peer (identified by host:port, or by DTLS connection ID when used), so that each peer's handshake and data are processed on its own session; sending to and receiving from each peer via the same server socket must reach the right client, and one client closing or timing out must not disturb the other client's session.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p qemu_x86 -T tests/net/socket/tls -s tests/net/socket/tls/net.socket.tls -s net.socket.tls -O twister-out --no-clean -W

verification.reason: The core feature is described, but the hidden tests require several missing public names, configuration names, and observable error/session-count behaviours that can be added to the statement without revealing the implementation.

problems.detail: The hidden tests use ztls_get_session_count(void) with return type uint32_t to verify how many TLS/DTLS sessions are allocated, but the statement never names this function or its kind.

The tests check exact session-count semantics: a session context exists for each TLS/DTLS context even before handshake, a DTLS server allocates a separate session per handshaked peer, and a closed/timed-out peer releases only that peer's session while the server retains at least one session.

The tests expect specific observable results: POLLHUP for closed/timed-out server sessions, EAGAIN on nonblocking server recv when idle, ENOTCONN when sending to a peer whose session no longer exists, and ENOTCONN on the timed-out client.
The tests exercise CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_DTLS_TIMEOUT and CONFIG_MBEDTLS_SSL_DTLS_CONNECTION_ID enabled/disabled, but the statement does not give these configuration names or their meanings.

The statement says sessions may be identified by DTLS connection ID but does not specify the public setsockopt path (ZSOCK_TLS_DTLS_CID with ZSOCK_TLS_DTLS_CID_ENABLED / ZSOCK_TLS_DTLS_CID_SUPPORTED) or the required CID matching behaviour.
The hidden tests also include DTLS sendmsg behaviour tied to CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_DTLS_SENDMSG_BUF_SIZE and EMSGSIZE, which the statement does not mention.

leak_check.leak_detail: The phrase “use its existing active session” hints at an internal active-session concept, but it is high-level and can be reworded without losing the required behaviour.
leak_check.suggested_statement:
A DTLS server socket can only maintain a single client session at a time: it keeps one TLS/DTLS context per socket file descriptor, so a second peer connecting to the same server socket cannot establish its own handshake, and traffic from multiple peers is not routed independently. A DTLS server socket should be able to handle several clients concurrently, maintaining a separate TLS session per peer (identified by host:port, or by DTLS connection ID when used), so that each peer's handshake and data are processed on its own session; sending to and receiving from each peer via the same server socket must reach the right client, and one client closing or timing out must not disturb the other client's session.

The change must expose `uint32_t ztls_get_session_count(void)`, which returns the total number of currently allocated TLS/DTLS session contexts. A newly created TLS/DTLS socket has one session context. A DTLS server socket should allocate an additional session context only when it must serve a second distinct peer; it must retain at least one session context while the server socket remains open. A client close must release both the client's session context and the corresponding server-side session context. A server-side session timeout must release only the server-side session context; the client's own context may remain until the client closes or its own timeout occurs. The observable counts are therefore: with a server socket and two client sockets created, 3; after the first client handshake, still 3; after the second client handshake, 4; after one client is closed, 2; after both clients are closed, 1.

DTLS server session timeout must be governed by `CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_DTLS_TIMEOUT`. When a server-side session times out, or when a peer closes, the server socket must report `ZSOCK_POLLHUP` on a subsequent poll, and other sessions on the same server socket must remain usable. A client whose session is closed by the server must observe `ENOTCONN` from subsequent recv(). Non-blocking or timed-out recv()/recvfrom() on the server after the relevant session is gone should return `EAGAIN`.

When DTLS connection IDs are enabled (`CONFIG_MBEDTLS_SSL_DTLS_CONNECTION_ID`), a server must match an incoming packet to an existing session by CID even if the peer's host or port changes. A packet from the same peer after a rebind must not allocate a new session; sending from the server to the old address must fail with `ENOTCONN`, while sending to the new address must succeed. A different peer using the same address but a different CID must be assigned a new session.

Sending from the server to a peer address that has no matching session must fail with `ENOTCONN`.

The DTLS sendmsg() path must continue to accept a single-fragment message whose size exceeds the configured intermediate buffer and must not fail it with `EMSGSIZE` solely for that reason.
